title: Unsupported Systems, Networks, and Exposed Services

slides.title: Unsupported Systems, Networks, and Exposed Services
points: Attack surfaces grow when systems are unsupported, networks are insecure, ports are unnecessarily open, or devices retain default credentials.
Security+ Objective 2.2: explain common threat vectors and attack surfaces.

slides.title: Unsupported Systems and Applications
slides.teach: Systems or applications no longer receiving vendor updates or security fixes.

course.learn: Systems or applications no longer receiving vendor updates or security fixes.

breakdown.explanation: The vendor has stopped supporting it, so known flaws may remain unpatched.

course.why: Unsupported technology accumulates risk because newly discovered vulnerabilities may never be fixed.
course.example: A legacy operating system has a known vulnerability but no vendor patch exists.
course.check_q: What risk exists when a vendor no longer provides fixes?

slides.title: Wireless Networks
slides.teach: Wireless networks use radio communication and can be attacked through weak encryption, rogue access points, or poor configuration.

course.learn: Wireless networks use radio communication and can be attacked through weak encryption, rogue access points, or poor configuration.

breakdown.explanation: The network is reachable over radio rather than only through a cable.

course.why: Wireless expands the physical reach of the network beyond the building's wired ports.
course.example: An attacker connects through a poorly secured wireless access point from outside the office.
course.check_q: Which attack surface uses Wi-Fi radio communication?

slides.title: Wired Networks
slides.teach: Wired networks can be exposed when physical access, switch ports, segmentation, or port security are weak.

course.learn: Wired networks can be exposed when physical access, switch ports, segmentation, or port security are weak.

breakdown.explanation: The attacker gains or abuses a physical LAN connection.
Open wall jack, Rogue device on LAN

course.why: A physical connection can place an unauthorized device directly on the internal network.
course.example: A visitor plugs a rogue laptop into an unused wall jack.
course.check_q: Which network attack surface involves plugging into a LAN port?

slides.title: Bluetooth
slides.teach: Bluetooth is short-range wireless technology that can expose nearby devices through pairing abuse, weak configuration, or implementation flaws.

course.learn: Bluetooth is short-range wireless technology that can expose nearby devices through pairing abuse, weak configuration, or implementation flaws.

breakdown.explanation: The attack happens over short-range device-to-device wireless communication.

course.why: Bluetooth-enabled devices may accept connections or expose services to nearby attackers.
course.example: An attacker near a conference room attempts unauthorized Bluetooth pairing with company devices.
course.check_q: Which attack surface involves nearby pairing attempts?

slides.title: Open Service Ports
slides.teach: Open ports expose listening services that attackers can enumerate or exploit.

course.learn: Open ports expose listening services that attackers can enumerate or exploit.

breakdown.explanation: An open port is like a network door to a service.

course.why: Every unnecessary exposed service increases the attack surface.
course.example: RDP is exposed directly to the internet even though remote access is not required.
course.exam: Listening service exposed → OPEN SERVICE PORT.
course.check_q: What attack surface is created by an unnecessary listening service?

slides.title: Default Credentials
slides.teach: Factory or vendor-default usernames and passwords are predictable and often publicly known.

course.learn: Factory or vendor-default usernames and passwords are predictable and often publicly known.

breakdown.explanation: The device still uses the login it shipped with.

course.why: Attackers can easily try known default credentials during reconnaissance or automated attacks.
course.example: A router is compromised because the administrator never changed admin/admin.
course.exam: Factory login still active → DEFAULT CREDENTIALS.
course.check_q: What weakness exists when a device still uses its factory password?

blocks.title: Unsupported Systems, Networks, and Exposed Services comparison
Identify what is exposed
items: If the vendor no longer provides security updates, the system remains exposed to known flaws.
Example: A legacy OS has a known vulnerability but no fix.
The attack surface is the wireless network.
Example: An attacker connects through a poorly secured access point.
An open port exposes a service even when it is unnecessary.
Example: RDP is exposed directly to the internet.
Factory login still active → DEFAULT CREDENTIALS
Predictable preset credentials are an easy entry point.
Example: A router still uses admin/admin.
The attacker targets short-range Bluetooth connectivity.
Example: A device accepts unauthorized pairing attempts.

questions.q: A legacy operating system has a known vulnerability, but the vendor no longer provides patches. Which attack-surface issue is most relevant?
questions.explanation: Unsupported systems no longer receive vendor security fixes.

questions.q: An attacker connects to a poorly secured office access point from outside the building. Which attack surface is being exploited?
questions.explanation: The attacker is using Wi-Fi radio access.

questions.q: A visitor plugs a rogue laptop into an unused Ethernet wall jack and gains network access. Which attack surface is most relevant?
questions.explanation: The attacker uses a physical wired LAN connection.

questions.q: An attacker nearby repeatedly attempts unauthorized pairing with company devices. Which attack surface is being targeted?
questions.explanation: The scenario describes short-range Bluetooth pairing.

questions.q: An unused RDP service is reachable directly from the internet. Which attack-surface issue is most relevant?
questions.explanation: RDP is a listening service exposed through an open port.

questions.q: A router is compromised because it still uses the vendor's default administrator password. Which issue is this?
questions.explanation: The device retained a predictable factory login.
